summary: Provides simple procedures for IPv6 hosts to detect network attachment, assessing whether their current addressing or routing configuration is valid for a newly connected network, and procedures for routers supporting them.

eli5.summary: When you plug in or join a new network, your computer needs to know if its old settings still work. This gives it a quick way to check.

questions: how does ipv6 host know it changed networks
what is simple dna in ipv6
how does an ipv6 host detect network attachment
subtitle: How an IPv6 host quickly checks whether it has returned to a network it already knows.

tldr.problem: When an IPv6 host connects to a network, it needs to know fast whether its existing addresses and configuration are still valid, without waiting on slow standard router advertisements.
tldr.mechanism: On a link-up indication the host marks addresses inoperable, sends a multicast Router Solicitation, and in parallel unicasts Neighbor Solicitations to routers recorded in its Simple DNA address table (SDAT). A reply from a known router marks its addresses operable again.
tldr.outcome: Routers need no changes, the worst case is no slower than standard neighbor discovery, and false positives are not acceptable while false negatives are.

facts.label: NS retransmissions
facts.value: No more than twice (SHOULD NOT exceed)

facts.label: Procedure rate limit
facts.value: Not more than once a second

sections.title: Goals and Scope
sections.content:
Hosts need a simple, reliable way to tell whether they have moved to a network they were recently connected to. Simple DNA (Detecting Network Attachment) uses router and neighbor discovery messages to collect reachability and configuration information. If the host has reattached to a link where it still has valid addresses, it can keep using them until confirmed by Neighbor Discovery or DHCPv6.

The goals are: routers do not have to be modified, common cases are optimized, worst-case latency equals standard neighbor discovery, false positives are not acceptable, and false negatives are acceptable. A false negative just means the host acquires fresh configuration.

It supports addresses from stateless address autoconfiguration (RFC 4862) or DHCPv6 (RFC 3315), but not manually configured addresses.
sections.eli5: The goal is to be quick when you are back somewhere familiar, never slower than normal, and never to wrongly think you are home when you are not.

sections.title: How the Approach Works
sections.content:
Earlier methods asked whether the host was still on the same link. Simple DNA instead probes each previously known router and decides whether to use the information learned from that router. This lets a host move among a small set of known links efficiently.

After a link-layer "up" indication, the host combines unicast Neighbor Solicitations (NSs) with a multicast Router Solicitation (RS). Standard routers delay a Router Advertisement by up to 500 ms and limit consecutive multicast RAs to one every 3 seconds, giving a worst case of 3.5 seconds without packet loss. A unicast NS to a known router avoids that wait.

If the host moves to a completely new link, performance is identical to standard neighbor discovery, though old addresses are flushed immediately instead of timing out.
sections.eli5: Instead of shouting to the whole street and waiting, you knock on the doors of the neighbors you already know. If one answers, you are home.

sections.title: The Simple DNA Address Table
sections.content:
The host keeps a Simple DNA address table (SDAT) for each interface. Entries are indexed by the router identifier, the router's link-local address plus its link-layer address. An entry holds the addresses of the router, a D-Flag (0 for SLAAC, 1 for DHCPv6), the host's IPv6 address with its lifetimes, and an O-Flag saying whether the address is operable.

SLAAC entries also store the prefix and an S-Flag recording whether SEND secured the Router Advertisement. DHCPv6 entries store the DUID, the IAID, an IA_NA/IA_TA flag and configuration such as DNS and NTP server addresses.

The host adds SDAT entries when it processes a Router Advertisement from an unknown router, and creates one entry per on-link router after DHCPv6 assigns an address. It may discard older entries when attaching to a new network.
sections.eli5: The table is a notebook of the routers you have met, with their names and the settings you got from each one.

sections.title: Host Procedure After Link-Up
sections.content:
On a link-layer indication the host MUST mark all non-tentative addresses inoperable until detection finishes, and MUST set Neighbor Cache entries for routers on its Default Router List to STALE. It SHOULD immediately send one Router Solicitation to the all-routers multicast address from a link-local source address.

For each router in the SDAT that has at least one valid address, counted once, the host MUST send a unicast NS to that router's link-local address with the router's stored link-layer address as the link-layer destination. It MUST NOT probe routers with no valid address in the SDAT. Both messages use Hop Limit 255. The NS probes SHOULD run in parallel with the RS, and an implementation SHOULD limit probing to at most six previously seen routers. The host also starts a DHCPv6 exchange to check DHCPv6 addresses.

When a Neighbor Advertisement arrives, the host MUST verify that both the IPv6 and link-layer addresses of the router match, then mark that router's addresses operable. When a Router Advertisement arrives, it marks that router's addresses inoperable and processes the RA normally.
sections.eli5: When you reach a place, you call out to everyone, and you also quietly check on the helpers you remember. If a remembered helper answers properly, you trust your old settings again.

sections.title: Conflicts, Retransmission and Next Steps
sections.content:
If the NS/NA result and the RS/RA result for the same router disagree, the RS/RA result is definitive. The exception is when the NA was secured with SEND and the RA was not: the host MUST wait SEND_NA_GRACE_TIME, 40 milliseconds, for a SEND-secured RA. For DHCPv6 addresses, the DHCPv6 result beats the NS result.

After confirming a router with an NS/NA pair, the host SHOULD rejoin solicited-node multicast groups for addresses it keeps and select a default router. It SHOULD NOT run duplicate address detection on addresses confirmed operable. If an NS probe did not complete, or the RS probe returned different prefixes than the SDAT, the host MUST begin normal address configuration.

Aggressive retransmission of NSs has little value. An implementation SHOULD NOT retransmit an NS more than twice, MUST cancel pending NS retransmissions after any NS response, and SHOULD NOT run the procedure more than once a second.
sections.eli5: If two answers disagree, trust the one from the router's own announcement. Do not keep knocking forever, and do not run back and forth more than once a second.

sections.title: Relationship to DNAv4
sections.content:
RFC 4436 (DNAv4) optimizes reattachment to a previously used IPv4 network by reusing a still-valid configuration. Simple DNA shares the goal of minimizing handover latency but uses different steps, and it also supports stateless autoconfiguration besides DHCPv6.

Appendix A explains why manually assigned addresses are excluded. Lost probes there could leave the host with no address, which would need aggressive retransmission. Moving between a manually addressed network and a dynamic one could also lead the host to take a dynamic address by mistake. Using manual addressing with Simple DNA is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: There is a similar trick for the older address system. This one is built for the newer system, and it does not try to help with addresses typed in by hand.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
After a link-up indication a host may receive Router Advertisements from non-SEND devices. The host's current SEND-secured router information must not be replaced by an attacker spoofing an RA to fake a link change. So the host SHOULD send an NS to the existing SEND router at link-up, and SHOULD ensure unsecured router information does not delete existing SEND state within MIN_DELAY_BETWEEN_RAS. If the default router is SEND-secured, it SHOULD wait SEND_NA_GRACE_TIME before adopting a new one.

Even valid SEND signatures do not prove authorization, so a host SHOULD NOT treat a router as secure until authorization delegation discovery succeeds. Without SEND or similar, DNA does not authenticate routers or the network, so the host MUST NOT make security-sensitive decisions from DNA alone, such as deciding it moved from an untrusted to a trusted network.
sections.eli5: A stranger could pretend to be your usual helper. So never decide a place is safe just because someone answered the door.
